Definition: to be (causatively, make) bitter (or unpleasant); (figuratively) to rebel (or resist; causatively, to provoke)
BiblicalUsage: mârâh is to be bitter, and figuratively to rebel and resist. In 1 Samuel 12:14 Samuel says that if Israel will not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, they and their king shall continue following Him, and in 1 Kings 13:21 the man of God is judged because he disobeyed the mouth of the LORD. In Hosea 13:16 Samaria shall become desolate because she has rebelled against her God. The word is bitterness that turns into disobedience.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mârâh shows me that bitterness and rebellion are the same root in the heart. I hold that the cure for both is to obey the voice I have been resisting.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
